summary: Queen Alia International Airport (AMM) is Jordan's main international gateway, located approximately 32 km south of central Amman in the city of Zizya. Named after Queen Alia, the third wife of King Hussein, the airport underwent a major expansion completed in 2013 with a striking terminal designed by Foster + Partners. It serves as the primary hub for Royal Jordanian Airlines and has repeatedly been recognized as one of the best airports in the Middle East by Skytrax and other industry bodies.
faqs:
Q: How far is Queen Alia International Airport from downtown Amman?
A: The airport is roughly 30-35 km south of central Amman, and the journey typically takes 45-60 minutes by car depending on traffic.

Q: Does the airport have free Wi-Fi?
A: Yes, complimentary Wi-Fi is available throughout both terminals for passengers and visitors.

Q: How many terminals does AMM have?
A: The airport operates two main passenger terminals: Terminal 1 handles international and most commercial flights, while Terminal 2 is primarily used by low-cost and regional carriers.

Q: Are there duty-free shops at the airport?
A: Yes, Queen Alia offers extensive duty-free shopping featuring local products like Jordanian olive oil, Dead Sea cosmetics, and souvenirs, alongside international brands.
transport_tips: The Airport Express bus (Sarakata) runs between AMM and Amman's Abdali area roughly every 30 minutes and is the most affordable option into the city. Official white airport taxis are available 24/7 at clearly marked ranks outside the arrivals hall; confirm the fare before departure as the journey can cost around 20-30 JOD. Ride-hailing apps like Careem and Uber also operate reliably at the airport and often provide fixed fares that avoid negotiation.
local_tip: Pick up a Jordan Pass online before your flight if you plan to visit Petra or other major sites—it includes the tourist visa fee for most nationalities, which can save you money and time at immigration, and gets stamped at the airport on arrival.
